A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDDP research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching appendix sections across the insertion of A.10 and subsequent renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic concept-recovery experiments, evaluations on five vision classifiers, ablations, and a chess-watermark model-correction experiment, with additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results. Its new human-evaluation discussion does not report a participant study.

M1.justification: Directional clustering, signal-vector estimation, loss functions, uncertainty-region alignment, and intervention procedures are unchanged. The added optimization sentence in A.7 reiterates the existing Augmented Lagrangian approach.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same synthetic task, Broden/Broden-Action evaluations, classifiers trained on Places365, ImageNet, and Moments in Time, and chess-watermark scenarios. No new population, domain, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: PCA, NMF, and Natural in the main comparisons; IBD and Pattern-CAVs in supervised comparisons; and UIBE/CBE in appendix Tables 25–26. NMF remains excluded for EfficientNet.

E3.justification: Detailed protocols, metric definitions, splits, sampling, and budgets match. However, new Appendix A.10 lists an undefined S3 metric without corresponding definitions or results. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is an editorial error or a newly reported evaluation metric.

E4.justification: The synthetic estimator tests, dreaming-based faithfulness analyses, loss ablations, margin sweeps, and application case studies retain the same questions and evidence. A.10 adds explanatory discussion, not a new supplementary experiment.

E5.justification: Both retain means and standard deviations across concept detectors, the RCAV label-permutation procedure with 100 noise directions, and Bonferroni correction. No repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results are unchanged, but v2 A.13/v3 A.14 revises the ResNet18 margin-sweep finding. Instead of describing S2 improvement for EDDP-U and slight deterioration for EDDP-C, v3 describes broadly similar S2 and mostly improving S1 for both when the margin decreases.

T1.justification: The signal-distractor model, mathematical assumptions, loss definitions, uncertainty-region derivations, and concept-contribution mathematics remain unchanged, including their appendix derivations.

C1.justification: The central method, effectiveness, and application claims are retained. Naming baselines and foregrounding the concept-count and SAE-comparison boundaries in the introduction restate scope already documented in v2 Sections 7.5 and 8.

C2.justification: New A.10 interprets alignment with human-produced annotations as implicit human evaluation and describes CLIP as a proxy for human semantic judgment. It explicitly acknowledges the absence of participants but adds no direct validation of these proxy interpretations.

D1.justification: Training stages, hyperparameters, schedules, implementation instructions, and computational-resource disclosures are retained. A.7's added Augmented Lagrangian preference repeats information already supplied in v2's method and experimental details.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning are retained. Section 2.1 foregrounds class-conditioned methods and gradient re-ranking already discussed in v2 A.12; the SAE comparison boundary was already stated in v2 Section 8.

P1.justification: v3 adds introductory clarification, Appendix A.10, and funding acknowledgments; edits prose; and renames experiment subsections from Analysis to Case Study. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: All 52 figures and 30 tables are retained, with layout reflow and relocated floats. Table 17 corrects EDDP-C's S1 best-value highlighting from 46.01 to 46.3, without changing either numerical value.

improvement.justification: Earlier visibility of the comparison boundaries and corrected best-value highlighting in Table 17 modestly improve clarity and presentation accuracy. The scientific evidence remains essentially unchanged. The new human-evaluation discussion adds rationale, but its unvalidated proxy claims and unexplained S3 reference limit its benefit.
